name: Survival Analysis Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in survival analysis work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in survival analysis work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Surface known limitations of a chosen survival analysis approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
2. Prefer the simplest survival analysis approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
3. When survival analysis decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
4. Keep survival analysis outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. When multiple survival analysis strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
6. Measure before optimizing any survival analysis bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. Prefer explicit, readable survival analysis solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
8. Validate survival analysis outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. When survival analysis guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
10. Document any non-obvious survival analysis decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
11. Check that survival analysis terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting survival analysis assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not silently drop survival analysis edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of survival analysis correctness.
- Avoid introducing new survival analysis abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated survival analysis concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about survival analysis over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
